newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power firm, seen surging Thurs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power firm, seen surging Thurs.

text.p: The current cold snap in the northeastern U.S. continued to support the region's spot bulk power market Wednesday, while players anticipate higher prices Thursday ahead of even chillier temperatures by this weekend.
"It might go up a couple of bucks," said a Houston power marketer, predicting Thursday's price movement.
Some market participants showed keen interests to lock up power deliveries through Tuesday, but others were reluctant to commit until they see Thursday's load projection for Friday through Tuesday.
The latest forecast indicated an Arctic air mass would push into the Northeast Thursday night, pushing temperatures 15-30 degrees Fahrenheit below normal.
In parts of upstate New York, night temperatures were forecast to plunge below zero to the -5 to -10 degree range.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices (including transmission costs) for Thursday delivery in the eastern part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) were valued near $34.50-$35.50, firmer than Tuesday's $32.00-$35.00 for Wednesday.
Off-peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in eastern NYPP remained in a $22.00-$24.00 range.
In western NYPP, peak, non-firm power for Thursday stayed at $28.00-$29.00 and Friday near $30.00, compared with Tuesday's $28.00-$29.00 for delivery today.
Western NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Thursday was again discussed at $15.00-$16.00, and edged up to $16.00-$17.00 for Friday delivery.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for day-ahead delivery at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border stood at $34.00-$36.00/MWh, flat from Tuesday.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for next-day delivery to the NU border remained at $22.00-$26.00.
Day-ahead electricity for peak, non-firm delivery at the Quebec-Northeast border stayed at $24.00-$25.00/MWh for Thursday and rose to $27.00-$28.00 for Friday.

Swing natural gas prices rebounded from Tuesday's drop on the outlook of plunging temperatures this weekend. Next-day gas deliveries at the New York City gate rallied 75 cents to the $5.00 per million British thermal unit level from Tuesday's $4.25 mark.
